questions.question: 8 men can complete a job in 20 days. 8 women can complete the same job in 32 days. In how many days will 5 men and 8 women together complete the same job?
questions.solution:

Work Equivalence: 8M × 20 = 8W × 32 ⇒ 20M = 32W ⇒ 5M = 8W.

Convert required group to women: 5M + 8W = 8W + 8W = 16W.

Inverse relation: If 8 women take 32 days, then 16 women (double people) take half the time.

Required days = 32 ÷ 2 = 16 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Efficiency of 8 Men = 160 ÷ 20 = 8 units/day ⇒ Efficiency of 1 Man = 1 unit/day.

questions.question: Since the mass of the Moon is less than that of the Earth, what can be said about the weight of an object on the Moon compared to its weight on Earth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Less on the Moon**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Weight** is defined as the **gravitational force** with which a celestial body (like Earth or the Moon) attracts an object towards its center.
 
• The **weight** of an object is directly proportional to the **acceleration due to gravity (g)** of the planet or moon it is on, expressed by the relationship: Weight = mass × g.
 
• The value of **g** depends on the **mass** (M) and **radius** (R) of the celestial body, according to the formula g = (G times M)/(R²) .
 
• Since the **mass of the Moon** is approximately 1/81 times that of the Earth and its **radius** is about 1/4 times that of the Earth, the **gravitational pull** on the Moon is much weaker.
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity on the Moon** is approximately **1/6th** (about 1.625 m/s²) of the acceleration due to gravity on **Earth** (about 9.8 m/s²).
 
• Therefore, an object will weigh **significantly less** on the Moon than it does on Earth, even though its **mass** remains unchanged.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mass** is an **intrinsic property** of an object and represents the amount of matter it contains; it remains **constant** regardless of location in the universe.
 
• The **SI unit of weight** is the **Newton (N)** because it is a force, while the **SI unit of mass** is the **Kilogram (kg)**.
 
• If a person has a mass of 60 kg, their weight on **Earth** would be approximately 588 N, but their weight on the **Moon** would be only about 98 N.
 
• The **Moon's gravity** is enough to cause **tides** on Earth but is too weak to hold a significant **atmosphere**.

questions.question: Karan and Arjun start a business by investing ₹45,000 and ₹50,000, respectively. Karan invests his money for 4 months and Arjun for 10 months. At the end of the year, 20% of the total profit is ₹30,600. What is Arjun’s share of the profit (in ₹)?

Total profit units = 9 + 25 = 34 units.

Total profit amount = 30,600 × 5 = 1,53,000 (since 20% is 30,600).

34 units = 1,53,000 ⇒ 1 unit = 4,500.

Arjun's share = 25 × 4,500 = 1,12,500.

**∴ The correct answer is 1,12,500.**

Arjun's investment (Cₐ) = ₹50,000, Time (Tₐ) = 10 months

⇒ Total Profit = 30,600 × (100 ÷ 20) = 30,600 × 5 = ₹1,53,000

⇒ Total ratio units = 9 + 25 = 34 units

⇒ Arjun's share = (25 ÷ 34) × 1,53,000

⇒ Arjun's share = 25 × 4,500 = ₹1,12,500

**∴ The correct answer is 1,12,500.**

questions.question: Thicker muscular walls are present in the ventricles of the heart due to which of the following reasons?

options.text: To store blood before it enters the atria
To pump blood with high pressure
To receive blood from the body and lungs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To pump blood with high pressure**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **ventricles** of the heart have thicker muscular walls compared to the **atria** because they are responsible for pumping blood out of the heart to various organs.
 
• The **Left Ventricle** has the thickest wall because it must pump **oxygenated blood** to the entire body through the **aorta**, requiring high pressure to ensure the blood reaches distal tissues.
 
• The **Right Ventricle** pumps **deoxygenated blood** to the **lungs** via the **pulmonary artery**; while its walls are thicker than the atria, they are thinner than the left ventricle because the lungs are located close to the heart.
 
• In contrast, the **atria** only need to pump blood into the ventricles located directly below them, which requires much less pressure and force, resulting in thinner walls.
 
• Option 1 is incorrect because blood flows from the atria to the ventricles, not the other way around.
 
• Option 3 is incorrect because receiving blood is the primary function of the **atria** (Right Atrium receives blood from the body, Left Atrium receives blood from the lungs).
 
• Option 4 is incorrect because the heartbeat and rhythm are controlled by the **Sinoatrial (SA) node**, also known as the **natural pacemaker**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The human heart is a **four-chambered** muscular organ protected by a double-walled sac called the **pericardium**.
 
• The **Septum** is a muscular wall that separates the right side (deoxygenated blood) from the left side (oxygenated blood) to prevent mixing.
 
• **Valves** (like the **mitral** and **tricuspid** valves) are present between the chambers to ensure **unidirectional blood flow** and prevent backflow.
 
• The thickness of the left ventricular wall is approximately three times that of the right ventricular wall, reflecting the higher resistance of the **systemic circulation** compared to the **pulmonary circulation**.

questions.question:
A question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and select the most appropriate answer.

**Question:**

Among 5 poles, I, L, O, M and D each having a different height, which pole is the tallest?

**Statements:**

(I) I is taller than only two poles. L is taller than D and no pole has height between L and D.

(II) M is taller than D.

options.text: Data in both statements I and II together are not sufficient to answer the question.
Data in both statements I and II together (and not statement I alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question.
Data in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement I is not.
Data in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement II is not.

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

I. I is taller than only two poles. L is taller than D and no pole has height between them.

II. M is taller than D.

Analysis:

I. From Statement I →

I is taller than only two poles ⇒ I is at Rank 3.

L is taller than D and no pole is between them ⇒ L and D are consecutive in height.

Since, I is at Rank 3, the two poles taller than I must occupy Rank 1 and Rank 2.

Therefore, L and D must be above I, with L above D.

So, the order becomes: L > D > I

Hence, L is the tallest pole.

Statement I alone is sufficient.

II. From Statement II → We get M > D, but no comparison with I, L, or O → Not sufficient.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

questions.question: Find the mean proportional between 36 and 81.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Mean Proportional (MP) = √(Number₁ × Number₂)

Given numbers: 36 and 81

MP = √(36 × 81) = 6 × 9 = 54

**∴ The correct answer is 54.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number (a) = 36

Second number (b) = 81

**Formula Used:**

If x is the mean proportional between a and b, then a : x :: x : b, which implies x² = a × b or x = √(ab).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d78cc1e7612c68f5a0586d7fc6c8ff645e7c5db05a684911acd539dd267cec9c.png] 

⇒ Let the mean proportional be x.

⇒ 36/x = x/81

⇒ x² = 36 × 81

⇒ x = √(36 × 81)

⇒ x = √2916

⇒ x = 54

**∴ The correct answer is 54.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Third Proportional

If three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion (a:b = b:c), then c is the third proportional. Formula: c = b²/a.

Fourth Proportional

If four numbers a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a:b = c:d), then d is the fourth proportional. Formula: d = (b × c)/a.

Continued Proportion

A sequence of numbers is in continued proportion if the ratio of any two consecutive terms is constant. Example: a/b = b/c = c/d.

questions.question: A trader marks a product at ₹2,000. He offers two successive discounts of 20% and 10% to a customer. Find the single equivalent discount percentage and the selling price of the product.

Final Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − Net discount)%

SP = 2000 × (72/100) = ₹1,440

**∴ The correct answer is 28%, ₹1,440.**

⇒ Total Discount amount = 2000 − 1440 = ₹560

⇒ Single Equivalent Discount % = (560/2000) × 100 = 28%

questions.question: In onion peel and human cheek cells, the lightly stained region enclosed by the cell membrane is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cytoplasm**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **cytoplasm** is the jelly-like substance that fills the cell and is enclosed by the **cell membrane**. In both **onion peel cells** (plant) and **human cheek cells** (animal), it represents the **lightly stained region** observed under a microscope.
 
• During the staining process (using dyes like **Iodine** or **Methylene Blue**), different parts of the cell absorb the stain with varying intensities. The **nucleus** is a dense structure that stains very darkly, while the **cytoplasm** is less dense and appears much lighter.
 
• The **cytoplasm** acts as the primary site for most **metabolic activities** and chemical reactions within the cell. It contains various **cell organelles** such as mitochondria, ribosomes, and endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• In **human cheek cells**, the cytoplasm is spread throughout the cell, whereas in **onion peel cells**, a large central **vacuole** often pushes the cytoplasm and the nucleus toward the periphery (edge) of the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Wall**: This is a rigid outer covering found only in **plant cells** like onion peel. It is located outside the **cell membrane** and provides protection and structural support. **Human cheek cells** do not have a cell wall.
 
• **Nucleus**: Often referred to as the **control center** of the cell, it contains the **genetic material** (DNA). It is usually the most prominent and **darkly stained** organelle when viewed under a light microscope.
 
• **Vacuole**: These are membrane-bound storage sacs. In **plant cells**, vacuoles are typically very large and occupy a significant portion of the cell volume, while in **animal cells**, they are much smaller or temporary.
 
• **Methylene Blue** is a common stain used for **animal cells** (cheek cells) to make the nucleus and cytoplasm visible, while **Iodine solution** or **Safranin** is frequently used for **plant cells** (onion peel).

questions.question: A man goes from place A to B at a speed of 12 km/h and returns from B to A at a speed of 3 km/h using the same route. The average speed (km/h) for the whole journey is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When distances are equal, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) / (S₁ + S₂)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 12 × 3) / (12 + 3)

⇒ Average Speed = 72 / 15 = 4.8 kmph

⇒ 4.8 kmph = 24/5 = 4 4/5 kmph

**∴ The correct answer is 4.8 kmph.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Speed from A to B = 12 kmph, Speed from B to A = 3 kmph.

Formula Used: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a96a3213cfe32e183f685787daa790a3f1ee3dadfb2944f6d67d3abe311a96d7.png] 

⇒ Let the distance between A and B be 12 km (LCM of 12 and 3).

⇒ Time taken to travel from A to B = Distance ÷ Speed = 12 / 12 = 1 hour.

⇒ Time taken to travel from B to A = Distance ÷ Speed = 12 / 3 = 4 hours.

⇒ Total Distance = 12 + 12 = 24 km.

⇒ Total Time = 1 + 4 = 5 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = 24 / 5 = 4.8 kmph.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.8 kmph.**

If a person covers three equal distances at speeds x, y, and z, then Average Speed = (3xyz) / (xy + yz + zx).

To convert speed from kmph to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to kmph, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

If two objects move in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂. In the same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

questions.question: A student's marks were incorrectly entered as 70 instead of 91. Due to this, the average marks of the class got decreased by (7)/(3) . What is the number of students in the class?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total difference in marks = 91 − 70 = 21.

Number of students = (Total mark difference) ÷ (Average change).

Number of students = 21 ÷ (7/3).

Number of students = 21 × (3/7) = 3 × 3 = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Correct marks = 91

Incorrect marks = 70

Decrease in average = 7/3

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of values) ÷ (Total number of values)

Total Number of Students = (Net change in sum) ÷ (Change in average)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/37bc0ff5b764f4b3326f68195df7ddf0ea7e0ebf007502accc5bd5dd1e7059b1.png] 

⇒ Let the number of students in the class be n.

⇒ Total Marks Error = Correct Marks − Incorrect Marks

⇒ Total Marks Error = 91 − 70 = 21

⇒ Decrease in Average = (Total Marks Error) ÷ n

⇒ 7/3 = 21 ÷ n

⇒ n = (21 × 3) ÷ 7

⇒ n = 3 × 3 = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Change in Average

The change in average is equal to the net change in the sum divided by the total number of observations: ΔAvg = ΔSum ÷ n.

Average Concept

Average is the central value of a set of numbers, calculated by Sum ÷ Count.

Weighted Average

When two groups are combined, the new average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question: Among the following, which structure is cup shaped at one end of coiled tube in kidney?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bowman's capsule**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **nephron** is the structural and functional unit of the **kidney**. Each kidney contains approximately 1 million complex tubular structures called nephrons.
 
• A nephron consists of two main parts: the **glomerulus** and the **renal tubule**.
 
• The renal tubule begins with a double-walled **cup-like structure** called **Bowman’s capsule**, which encloses the **glomerulus**.
 
• The **glomerulus** is a tuft of capillaries formed by the **afferent arteriole** (a fine branch of the renal artery). Blood is filtered through the glomerular capillaries into the Bowman's capsule.
 
• The **Malpighian body** or **renal corpuscle** is the collective term for the glomerulus and Bowman's capsule.
 
• **Loop of Henle** is a **hairpin-shaped** (U-shaped) part of the renal tubule that follows the proximal convoluted tubule; it is not cup-shaped.
 
• The **Collecting duct** is a long straight tube where the **Distal Convoluted Tubules (DCT)** of many nephrons open.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The epithelial cells of Bowman’s capsule are called **podocytes**. These are arranged in an intricate manner so as to leave some minute spaces called **filtration slits** or **slit pores**.
 
• The process of **ultrafiltration** occurs in the renal corpuscle, where blood is filtered so finely that almost all the constituents of the plasma except the proteins pass into the lumen of the Bowman’s capsule.
 
• The renal tubule continues beyond the capsule to form the **Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT)**, then the **Henle’s loop**, and finally the **Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT)**.
 
• The **kidneys** play a vital role in **osmoregulation** and the excretion of nitrogenous wastes like **urea**.

questions.question: A metal object exposed to a humid environment starts corroding. Which of the following methods would be the most effective and long-lasting in preventing corrosion?

options.text: Applying a single coat of paint
Coating with a more reactive metal like zinc
Wrapping the metal with a dry cloth to prevent moisture exposure
Periodically wiping the surface with oil

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coating with a more reactive metal like zinc**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Galvanization** is the process of applying a protective **zinc coating** to steel or iron to prevent rusting. This is considered the most effective and long-lasting method because it provides **sacrificial protection**.
 
• Zinc is **more reactive** than iron (higher in the **reactivity series**). This means that the zinc layer will oxidize first when exposed to the environment, acting as a **sacrificial anode**.
 
• Unlike paint or oil, which only act as a physical barrier, galvanization remains effective even if the coating is **scratched** or slightly damaged, as the surrounding zinc will still corrode preferentially to protect the exposed iron.
 
• **Applying paint** or **periodically wiping with oil** are known as **barrier methods**. While they prevent moisture and oxygen from reaching the metal, they are temporary and fail as soon as the coat is chipped, scratched, or wears off.
 
• **Wrapping the metal with a dry cloth** is highly ineffective in a **humid environment** because fabric can trap moisture against the metal surface, potentially accelerating corrosion rather than preventing it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Corrosion** is a natural process that converts a refined metal into a more chemically stable form, such as its **oxide**, hydroxide, or sulfide. Rusting specifically refers to the corrosion of **iron**.
 
• The chemical formula for rust is typically represented as Fe₂O₃ · xH₂O (**hydrated iron (III) oxide**).
 
• **Cathodic Protection** is a similar technique where a more active metal like **magnesium** or zinc is connected to the structure to be protected (like ship hulls or underground pipelines).
 
• **Alloying** is another permanent method to prevent corrosion; for example, **Stainless Steel** is made by mixing iron with **chromium** and nickel, which forms a thin, invisible layer of chromium oxide that prevents further reaction.
 
• Environmental factors like **saltwater** (electrolytes) and high **humidity** significantly increase the rate of corrosion.

questions.question:
In the following figure, RS ∥ TU. Find the value of ∠PQR − ∠PRQ, if ∠QTU + ∠PRQ = 130° and ∠RPQ = 80°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e48edf883df74ce81564fa0a3193d9c35f7084ad87df452ebc41fc7da079b8f3.png]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In ΔPQR, sum of angles ∠PQR + ∠PRQ = 180° − 80° = 100°.

Given RS || TU, the consecutive interior angles ∠QTU + ∠PQR = 180°.

We are given ∠QTU + ∠PRQ = 130°.

Subtracting the equations: (∠QTU + ∠PQR) − (∠QTU + ∠PRQ) = 180° − 130°.

⇒ ∠PQR − ∠PRQ = 50°.

**∴ The correct answer is 50°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

RS || TU

∠QTU + ∠PRQ = 130°

∠RPQ = 80°

**Formula used:**

1. Sum of interior angles of a triangle = 180°.

2. Sum of consecutive interior angles between parallel lines = 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4ffdebf8edac5514f923794ad9ea118fed86cba4697c6e03fa75afdabe3d88c7.png] 

**Calculations:**

In ΔPQR:

⇒ ∠RPQ + ∠PQR + ∠PRQ = 180°

⇒ 80° + ∠PQR + ∠PRQ = 180°

⇒ ∠PQR + ∠PRQ = 100° ... (Eq. 1)

Since RS || TU and TQ acts as a transversal:

⇒ ∠QTU + ∠PQR = 180° (Consecutive interior angles)

⇒ ∠QTU = 180° − ∠PQR ... (Eq. 2)

Given in the question:

⇒ ∠QTU + ∠PRQ = 130°

Substitute ∠QTU from Eq. 2:

⇒ (180° − ∠PQR) + ∠PRQ = 130°

⇒ 180° − ∠PQR + ∠PRQ = 130°

⇒ 180° − 130° = ∠PQR − ∠PRQ

⇒ ∠PQR − ∠PRQ = 50°

**∴ The correct answer is 50°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Interior Angles

When two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, the sum of the interior angles on the same side is always 180°.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles in any triangle is constant and equals 180° (∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°).

Alternate Interior Angles

If a transversal intersects two parallel lines, the alternate interior angles are equal in magnitude.

⇒ ∠ALB = ∠PMQ = 90° (Since AL and PM are altitudes)

⇒ ∠B = ∠Q (Proven above)

⇒ ΔABL ∼ ΔPQM (By AA similarity criterion)

⇒ AL/PM = AB/PQ

⇒ AL/PM = 12/4

⇒ AL/PM = 3/1

**∴ The correct answer is 3:1.**

Similarity Ratios

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their corresponding sides is equal to the ratio of their corresponding perimeters, medians, and angle bisectors.

Area Ratio Property

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area₁/Area₂ = (Side₁/Side₂)².

AA Similarity Criterion

If two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another triangle, then the two triangles are similar.

questions.question: Which award, one of India’s highest honours in the livestock and dairy sector, was announced in November 2025?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Gopal Ratna Award** is one of the highest national awards in the field of **livestock and dairy sector** in **India**, designed to recognize and encourage stakeholders in this vital industry.
 
• For the year **2025**, the announcement and felicitation process is organized by the **Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying**, which functions under the **Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying**.
 
• The awards are traditionally conferred every year on **November 26**, a date celebrated as **National Milk Day** to honor the birth anniversary of **Dr. Verghese Kurien**, the architect of **India**'s **White Revolution**.

questions.question: A car falls off a ledge and drops to the ground in 0.6 s. Take g = 10 m/s². What is the car’s speed on striking the ground?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 m/s**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object falls off a surface or is dropped, its **initial velocity (u)** is considered **0 m/s**.
 
• The motion is a case of **free fall** under the influence of the **acceleration due to gravity (g)**, which is given as **10 m/s²**.
 
• The **time (t)** duration for the fall is **0.6 s**.
 
• To find the **final velocity (v)**, we use the **first equation of motion**: **v = u + at**.
 
• In the context of gravity, the formula becomes: **v = u + gt**.
 
• Substituting the values: **v = 0 + (10 × 0.6)**.
 
• The calculation results in **v = 6 m/s**. This is the speed at which the car strikes the ground.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **three standard equations of motion** for objects under **uniform acceleration** are:

 
 
• **v = u + at**
 
• s = ut + (1)/(2)at² 
 
• **v² = u² + 2as**
 
 
 
• The **height of the ledge (s)** can be calculated using the second equation: s = 0 + 1/2 × 10 × (0.6)² = 5 × 0.36 = **1.8 m**.
 
• The **average speed** of the car during the 0.6 s interval is (0 + 6) / 2 = **3 m/s**.
 
• The value of **acceleration due to gravity (g)** is approximately **9.8 m/s²** on the surface of the Earth, but **10 m/s²** is often used for easier calculation in physics problems.

questions.question: The apparent random wavering or flickering of objects seen through a turbulent stream of hot air rising above a fire or a radiator is due to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atmospheric refraction of light**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The air just above a fire or radiator becomes **hotter** than the air further up. Hot air is **less dense** (lighter) than the cooler air above it, and it has a **lower refractive index** than cool air.
 
• Because the physical conditions of the air are not stationary (the hot air rises and mixes with cool air), the **refractive index** of the medium through which the light passes is constantly changing.
 
• As the light from an object passes through these layers of air with **varying refractive indices**, its path is bent continuously and randomly.
 
• This causes the **apparent position** of the object to fluctuate, leading to the **wavering or flickering** effect. This phenomenon is a local-scale example of **atmospheric refraction**.
 
• **Diffraction of light** refers to the bending of light around the corners of an obstacle or aperture, which is not the cause here.
 
• **Dispersion of light** is the phenomenon of splitting white light into its constituent seven colors (like in a rainbow), which does not explain the wavering.
 
• **Reflection of light** is the bouncing back of light when it strikes a surface, which is also not responsible for this flickering effect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Twinkling of stars**: This is a similar effect caused by **atmospheric refraction** on a much larger scale as starlight passes through different layers of the Earth's atmosphere with varying densities and temperatures.
 
• **Mirage**: An optical illusion often seen in deserts or on hot roads, where water appears to be on the ground, is also caused by **total internal reflection** resulting from intense **atmospheric refraction** due to temperature gradients.
 
• **Refractive Index**: It is a measure of how much the **speed of light** is reduced inside a medium compared to a vacuum. It is temperature-dependent; as temperature increases, the density usually decreases, lowering the refractive index.
 
• **Advance sunrise and delayed sunset**: The Sun is visible to us about **2 minutes** before the actual sunrise and **2 minutes** after the actual sunset due to atmospheric refraction.

questions.question: The sum of the present ages of Kamlesh and Prathmesh is 52 years. After 2 years from now, Kamlesh's age will be three times that of Prathmesh's age. Kamlesh's present age (in years) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total age after 2 years = 52 + (2 persons × 2 years) = 56 years.

Ratio of Kamlesh to Prathmesh after 2 years = 3 : 1.

Sum of ratio parts = 3 + 1 = 4 units.

4 units → 56 years ∴ 1 unit → 14 years.

Kamlesh age after 2 years = 3 units × 14 = 42 years.

Kamlesh present age = 42 − 2 = 40 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of present ages of Kamlesh (K) and Prathmesh (P) = 52 years.

Condition: After 2 years, K + 2 = 3 × (P + 2).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3a2bfb81cd9709ace4eeeaefab8e0bf1e50b63798124722d890e6f40282ae71.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let Prathmesh's present age be P.

⇒ Kamlesh's present age K = 52 − P.

According to the problem, after 2 years:

⇒ (52 − P) + 2 = 3 × (P + 2)

⇒ 54 − P = 3P + 6

⇒ 3P + P = 54 − 6

⇒ 4P = 48

⇒ P = 12 years

⇒ K = 52 − 12 = 40 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

questions.question: 4% of a number is approximately what percentage of 18% of the same number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When comparing percentages of the same number, the number cancels out.

Required percentage = (First % value ÷ Second % value) × 100

Required percentage = (4 ÷ 18) × 100 = 2/9 × 100

Since 1/9 ≈ 11.11%, then 2/9 = 2 × 11.11% = 22.22%

**∴ The correct answer is 22.22%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0df58bd3e2cdeae42559a1bf097d6deb1b91fe1640155be05903fb5273db8dea.png] 

⇒ Let the number be x. ⇒ First value (A) = 4% of x = 4x/100 ⇒ Second value (B) = 18% of x = 18x/100 ⇒ Required % = (A ÷ B) × 100 ⇒ Required % = [(4x/100) ÷ (18x/100)] × 100 ⇒ Required % = (4 ÷ 18) × 100 ⇒ Required % = (2 ÷ 9) × 100 ⇒ Required % = 200 ÷ 9 ≈ 22.22%

**∴ The correct answer is 22.22%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Comparison Base

To find what percentage x is of y, the formula is (x ÷ y) × 100. Here y is the base or reference value.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

Reciprocal values like 1/9 = 11.11% and 1/11 = 9.09% are essential for solving competitive exam questions quickly.

Successive Percentage

If a number is changed by a% and then b%, the net effective change is [a + b + (ab/100)]%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells an item for ₹689.7 after giving two successive discounts of 75% and 34% on its marked price. Had he not given any discount, he would have earned a profit of 76%. What is the cost price (in ₹) of the item?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive discount multiplier = 0.25 × 0.66 = 0.165

Marked Price (MP) = 689.7 ÷ 0.165 = 4180

CP × (1 + 76/100) = MP (when no discount is given)

CP = 4180 ÷ 1.76 = 2375

**∴ The correct answer is 2375.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Selling Price (SP) = ₹689.7

Discounts = 75% and 34%

Profit without discount = 76%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/522906d15ad4839ed74e00df5c406e89216ea7762e782b128dc9410153fecdce.png] 

Formula used: SP = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100)

⇒ 689.7 = MP × (1 − 75/100) × (1 − 34/100)

⇒ 689.7 = MP × 25/100 × 66/100

⇒ 689.7 = MP × 1/4 × 33/50

⇒ MP = (689.7 × 200) / 33

⇒ MP = 20.9 × 200 = 4180

⇒ According to the condition, if discount is 0, SP = MP = 4180

⇒ At this price, Profit = 76%

⇒ CP × (100 + 76)/100 = 4180

⇒ CP × 176/100 = 4180

⇒ CP = (4180 × 100) / 176

⇒ CP = 2375

**∴ The correct answer is 2375.**

Successive Discount

Relation between CP and MP

CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%). This ratio is used when both profit and discount are given.

questions.question: The Attorney General of India is the highest law officer of the country appointed by whom?

options.text: The seniormost Judge of Supreme Court

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Attorney General of India** is appointed by the **President of India** under **Article 76(1)** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• He or she is the **highest law officer** in the country and serves as the primary legal advisor to the **Government of India**.
 
• To be eligible for the post, a person must be qualified to be appointed as a **Judge of the Supreme Court**, meaning they must be a citizen of **India** and have been a judge of a **High Court** for **5 years** or an advocate of a **High Court** for **10 years**.
 
• The term of office for the **Attorney General** is not fixed by the **Constitution**; the individual holds the office during the **pleasure of the President**.
 
• The **Attorney General** performs duties of a legal character that are assigned by the **President** and discharges functions conferred by the **Constitution** or any other law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rights in Parliament:** Under **Article 88** of the **Constitution**, the **Attorney General** has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha**, including joint sittings, but does **not have the right to vote**.
 
• **Right of Audience:** In the performance of official duties, the **Attorney General** has the **right of audience** in all courts within the territory of **India**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The first **Attorney General of India** was **M.C. Setalvad**, who served the longest term from **1950** to **1963**.
 
• **Assistance:** The **Attorney General** is assisted by the **Solicitor General of India** and several **Additional Solicitors General** to carry out legal responsibilities, although these latter posts are statutory and not constitutional.
 
• **Remuneration:** The remuneration of the **Attorney General** is not fixed by the **Constitution** but is determined by the **President of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Limitations:** The **Attorney General** should not advise or hold a brief against the **Government of India** and should not defend accused persons in **criminal prosecutions** without the permission of the **Government**.
 
• **Legal Practice:** Unlike many other government officials, the **Attorney General** is not a full-time counsel for the **Government** and is not debarred from **private legal practice**, provided there is no conflict of interest with the **Union of India**.
 
• **Resignation:** Conventionally, the **Attorney General** resigns when the **Council of Ministers** (the government) is dissolved or resigns, as they are appointed on its advice.
 
• **Article 143:** The **Attorney General** represents the **Government of India** in any reference made by the **President** to the **Supreme Court** under **Article 143** regarding matters of public importance or law.

questions.question: What property of gases allows them to fill any container completely?

options.text: Particles remain fixed and cannot move easily.
Particles move freely and have negligible attraction.
Particles occupy definite volume and definite shape.
Particles form strong bonds with container walls.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Particles move freely and have negligible attraction.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gases** consist of particles that are in a state of constant, **random motion** at high velocities. This rapid movement allows them to spread out and occupy every corner of any container they are placed in.
 
• The **intermolecular forces of attraction** between gas particles are **negligible** or extremely weak. Unlike **solids** or **liquids**, where particles are held together closely, gas particles move independently of one another.
 
• Because there is no significant force pulling the particles together, a gas does not have a **definite shape** or a **definite volume**. It expands spontaneously to fill the total volume available.
 
• The **kinetic energy** of the particles in a gas is high enough to overcome the attractive forces that would otherwise keep them clustered together, which is the primary reason for their high **fluidity** and **expansibility**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Compressibility:** Gases have large **intermolecular spaces**, making them highly compressible compared to solids and liquids. When pressure is applied, these spaces decrease, allowing the gas to fit into a smaller volume.
 
• **Diffusion:** Due to their high speed and large empty spaces, gases exhibit **diffusion**, where they mix rapidly with other gases. This is why the smell of perfume or food spreads quickly across a room.
 
• **Gas Pressure:** The **pressure** exerted by a gas is the result of the constant **collisions** of its particles against the walls of the container.
 
• **Kinetic Molecular Theory:** This scientific model explains that **ideal gas** particles are so small compared to the distance between them that their individual volume is considered negligible.
